body:
Rule. Run a design interview in a fixed sequence: clarify, size, sketch, deepen the riskiest cut, then reserve minutes to name the first thing that breaks.

Why it matters. Without a frame, candidates invent features and never size traffic. Interviewers grade whether you can spend the hour on purpose.

SAMPLE example. SAMPLE: you get a URL product. You spend the first chunk locking reads versus writes, sketch one happy path, then leave a closing block to say which hop fails first under load.

When to use. Use the frame whenever the prompt is open-ended system design and the clock is real.

When to refuse. Refuse diving into vendor logos or dark-mode extras before bounds exist. Refuse skipping the closing bottleneck sentence.
